name: ABS
notes: FP32, int8 and quantized int16 run CORE; quantized scaling requirements apply. Unquantized int16 uses Reference, which wraps -32768. FP16 requires ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16; without it preparation fails.

name: ADD
notes: Float identical-shape inputs support arbitrary rank. Optimized broadcasting supports rank <= 4; higher-rank FP32 uses Reference and FP16 is rejected. int32 follows the adapter reference path.

name: ARG_MAX
notes: int8 runs CORE, FP32 runs CORE with ARM_NN_ENABLE_F32 and FP16 with ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16, at rank 1..4 with INT32 axis/output and positive reduced extent; other configurations use Reference (FP16 is rejected). A NaN never wins and ties keep the first index.

name: ARG_MIN
notes: int8 runs CORE, FP32 runs CORE with ARM_NN_ENABLE_F32 and FP16 with ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16, at rank 1..4 with INT32 axis/output and positive reduced extent; other configurations use Reference (FP16 is rejected). A NaN never wins and ties keep the first index.

name: AVERAGE_POOL_2D
notes: Four-dimensional tensors; check filter/stride/padding and output dimensions. Kernel failure is returned to the application.

name: BATCH_MATMUL
notes: Check batch broadcasting, adjoint flags and quantized weight/activation combinations against the adapter.

name: CONCATENATION
notes: Optimized float paths support rank <= 4; higher-rank float inputs use Reference. Input/output type and quantization must agree.

name: CONV_2D
notes: Quantized weight/bias combinations are constrained. int4 weights use int8 activations. Float grouped convolution uses Reference for FP32 and is rejected for FP16.

name: COS
notes: Reference implementation in the HELIA adapter source; Float32 input/output.

name: DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D
notes: Quantized weight/bias combinations and depth multiplier are constrained. int4 is a weight type with int8 activations; it is not a general activation type.

name: DEQUANTIZE
notes: Output is FP32. FP16 means weight-storage widening, not FP16 computation; it calls arm_dequantize_f16_bits_f32 on every target, works without ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16, and matches the reference widening bit for bit at reset FPSCR: a NaN keeps its sign and payload and comes back quiet, on the MVE path too. On cores with an FPU but no MVE float16 (for example cortex-m4+fp) the widening runs on the FPU, so with FPSCR.DN (default NaN) set every NaN becomes 0x7FC00000.

name: DIV
notes: FP32 and FP16 run CORE for identical shapes and rank <= 4 broadcasts; other FP32 shapes use Reference and FP16 is rejected. int8 and int32 use Reference. FP16 requires ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16; without it preparation fails.

name: EQUAL
notes: Boolean output. Supported input types depend on the comparison; input shapes and broadcast rules must match.

name: FILL
notes: Constant dimensions and scalar fill value. Float APIs require CORE >= 7.33.0 and matching enabled feature.

name: FULLY_CONNECTED
notes: Quantized activation/weight/bias types must match a supported combination; includes int4 weights with int8 activations. Float paths require matching CORE features.

name: GATHER
notes: CORE >= 7.34.0. Native rank <= 4. Scalar indices use float native paths or int8 Reference; int16 rejects them. Higher-rank FP32/int8 use Reference; FP16/int16 reject.

name: GATHER_ND
notes: CORE >= 7.34.0. Native ranks <= 4 and positive index tuple width. Higher ranks and zero-width tuples use FP32/int8 Reference; FP16/int16 reject.

name: GREATER
notes: Boolean output. Check broadcast and operand types; no FP16 comparison branch.

name: GREATER_EQUAL
notes: Boolean output. Check broadcast and operand types; no FP16 comparison branch.

name: HARD_SWISH
notes: FP16 requires the CORE float feature; without it preparation fails. FP32 can use Reference.

name: LEAKY_RELU
notes: Float32 uses the reference path. No FP16 execution branch in this adapter.

name: LESS
notes: Boolean output. Check broadcast and operand types; no FP16 comparison branch.

name: LESS_EQUAL
notes: Boolean output. Check broadcast and operand types; no FP16 comparison branch.

name: LOG
notes: Reference implementation in the HELIA adapter source; Float32 input/output.

name: LOGICAL_NOT
notes: Reference boolean operation.

name: LOGISTIC
notes: int8 uses a lookup table; int16 and enabled floats have HELIA paths. NaN is not supported by the optimized float activation path.

name: MAXIMUM
notes: Optimized paths support rank <= 4. Higher-rank FP32/int8/int16 use Reference; FP16 is rejected. int32/int64 use Reference.

name: MAX_POOL_2D
notes: Four-dimensional tensors; check filter/stride/padding and output dimensions. Kernel failure is returned to the application.

name: MEAN
notes: Float optimized paths support rank <= 4 and axis sets; higher-rank FP32 uses Reference, FP16 is rejected. On every route and dtype, an output whose element count differs from the input's elements on the kept axes, an axis outside the input rank, or an input above rank 5, fails at Invoke; a scalar input ignores its axes, as in TFLite. See reduce_common.cc.

name: MINIMUM
notes: Optimized paths support rank <= 4. Higher-rank FP32/int8/int16 use Reference; FP16 is rejected. int32/int64 use Reference.

name: MUL
notes: Float identical-shape inputs support arbitrary rank. Optimized broadcasting supports rank <= 4; higher-rank FP32 uses Reference and FP16 is rejected. int32 follows the adapter reference path.

name: NEG
notes: FP32 and FP16 run CORE as sign-bit flips, NaN payloads kept. FP16 requires ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16; without it preparation fails.

name: NOT_EQUAL
notes: Boolean output. Supported input types depend on the comparison; input shapes and broadcast rules must match.

name: PACK
notes: Equal input shapes, including scalars. Float APIs require CORE >= 7.33.0 and matching enabled feature.

name: PAD
notes: FP16 requires four-dimensional tensors and the float feature. Padding values and output shape must match.

name: PADV2
notes: FP16 requires four-dimensional tensors and the float feature. Padding values and output shape must match.

name: PRELU
notes: int8, FP32 and FP16 run CORE when the output has the input shape, alpha broadcasts into it and rank <= 4; other FP32/int8 shapes use Reference and FP16 is rejected, except an empty FP16 tensor, which is a no-op. int16 uses Reference (int8 alpha). The output type must match the input type. FP16 requires ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16; without it preparation fails.

name: QUANTIZE
notes: Supported input/output pairs are specific: this type list does not imply all pairings. Registration is supplied by kernels/quantize.cc.

name: REDUCE_ALL
notes: Boolean reduction using Reference in reduce_common.cc. On every route and dtype, an output whose element count differs from the input's elements on the kept axes, or an axis outside the input rank, fails at Invoke; a scalar input ignores its axes, as in TFLite.

name: REDUCE_MAX
notes: int8/int16 run CORE at rank <= 4 with equal input/output quantization. FP32 runs CORE (arm_reduce_max_tflite_f32) at rank <= 4 with ARM_NN_ENABLE_F32 and Reference otherwise; FP16 runs CORE (arm_reduce_max_tflite_f16) at rank <= 4 and is rejected otherwise or without ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16. Both follow TFLite: a NaN is skipped, a window of NaNs, of -Inf only or an empty one gives the start value (-FLT_MAX, -65504 for FP16), and an empty axis list folds each element into it. On every route, dtype and rank, an output whose element count differs from the input's elements on the kept axes, or an axis outside the input rank, fails at Invoke; a scalar input ignores its axes, as in TFLite. Implementation is in reduce_common.cc.

name: REDUCE_MIN
notes: int8/int16 run CORE at rank <= 4 with equal input/output quantization. FP32 runs CORE (arm_reduce_min_tflite_f32) at rank <= 4 with ARM_NN_ENABLE_F32 and Reference otherwise; FP16 runs CORE (arm_reduce_min_tflite_f16) at rank <= 4 and is rejected otherwise or without ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16. Both follow TFLite: a NaN is skipped, a window of NaNs, of +Inf only or an empty one gives the start value (+FLT_MAX, +65504 for FP16), and an empty axis list folds each element into it. On every route, dtype and rank, an output whose element count differs from the input's elements on the kept axes, or an axis outside the input rank, fails at Invoke; a scalar input ignores its axes, as in TFLite. Implementation is in reduce_common.cc.

name: RELU
notes: Check activation bounds, tensor shape and quantization. Optimized float paths require the matching CORE feature.

name: RELU6
notes: Check activation bounds, tensor shape and quantization. Optimized float paths require the matching CORE feature.

name: RESHAPE
notes: Preserves storage and element count. FP16 storage works without float arithmetic enabled. Types listed here are representative fixed-width storage types.

name: RESIZE_NEAREST_NEIGHBOR
notes: Runs CORE when the output is [N, size[0], size[1], C], bit-exact with the reference for every align_corners/half_pixel_centers setting; other layers use Reference and FP16 is rejected. Needs an (height + width) int32 scratch. FP16 requires ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16; without it preparation fails.

name: RSQRT
notes: FP32 and FP16 run CORE; integer paths use Reference. FP16 requires CORE >= 7.33.0 and ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16; input/output shapes and types must match. A negative input gives the positive quiet NaN.

name: SIN
notes: Reference implementation in the HELIA adapter source; Float32 input/output.

name: SOFTMAX
notes: Optimized float path requires beta = 1. Other beta values use FP32 Reference or fail FP16 preparation. int8-to-int16 output has a dedicated registration.

name: SPLIT
notes: Constant axis and equal output extents. Float APIs require CORE >= 7.33.0 and corresponding enabled feature.

name: SPLIT_V
notes: Constant axis and split sizes; one inferred -1 size and zero-length pieces are allowed. Shapes/types/counts are checked during preparation. Float APIs require CORE >= 7.33.0.

name: SQRT
notes: FP32 and FP16 run CORE. FP16 requires CORE >= 7.33.0 and ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16; input/output shapes and types must match. A negative input gives the positive quiet NaN.

name: SQUARE
notes: Reference implementation in the HELIA adapter source; Float32 input/output.

name: SQUARED_DIFFERENCE
notes: int8/int16 run CORE for identical shapes and rank <= 4 broadcasts. FP32 runs CORE for identical shapes and uses Reference for broadcasts; on MVE float builds (cortex-m55) FP32 uses Reference throughout, because the CORE Helium path flushes subnormal results (AmbiqAI/ns-cmsis-nn#877). FP16 runs CORE for identical shapes and rejects broadcasts. int32 uses Reference. FP16 requires ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16; without it preparation fails.

name: SQUEEZE
notes: Bitwise storage copy; removes unit dimensions, checks matching byte counts and rejects strings. Input rank <= 8.

name: STRIDED_SLICE
notes: int8, int16 and int32 run CORE; FP32 runs CORE with ARM_NN_ENABLE_F32 and Reference without it; FP16 runs CORE with ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16 and fails preparation without it; bool uses Reference. Rank is limited to 4. For every type, an input axis above 2^30 or an input above INT32_MAX elements fails at Invoke, however small the slice; otherwise an empty slice writes nothing and succeeds, and a nonempty slice whose output element count differs from the slice's fails at Invoke. The input and output types must match.

name: SUB
notes: Float identical-shape inputs support arbitrary rank. Optimized broadcasting supports rank <= 4; higher-rank FP32 uses Reference and FP16 is rejected. int32 follows the adapter reference path.

name: SUM
notes: SUM is LiteRT REDUCE_SUM. Float optimized paths support rank <= 4 and axis sets; higher-rank FP32 uses Reference, FP16 is rejected. On every route and dtype, an output whose element count differs from the input's elements on the kept axes, an axis outside the input rank, or an input above rank 5, fails at Invoke; a scalar input ignores its axes, as in TFLite. See reduce_common.cc.

name: SVDF
notes: Data input is int8, FP32 or enabled FP16. int16 is a time-weight/state type, not a supported data input type. Variable state persists across invocations; weight types, rank and activation configuration are constrained.

name: TANH
notes: NaN is not supported by the optimized float activation path. Float support is build-gated.

name: TRANSPOSE
notes: Optimized rank <= 4. Higher ranks use Reference; FP16 has a bitwise storage fallback even with its float feature disabled.

name: TRANSPOSE_CONV
notes: Check output shape, padding and quantized weight/bias combinations. Float features are build-gated.

name: UNIDIRECTIONAL_SEQUENCE_LSTM
notes: Standard four-gate LSTM only. Preparation rejects peephole, projection, layer normalization and missing gates (CIFG), including FP32. Quantized inputs use int8 weights and int16 cell state. Preserve variable state across invocations.

name: UNPACK
notes: One output per selected axis element. Float APIs require CORE >= 7.33.0 and matching enabled feature.

name: ZEROS_LIKE
notes: Fills output storage with zero; no FP16 execution branch.
